comparator.name: Bachelor Medical Sciences and Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, Education Guide, learning-line, elective and final-project pages, checked 2026-10-05, identify Medical Sciences and Engineering as the medically oriented major within the three-year, 180-EC Biomedical Engineering bachelor. The official structure accounts for 105 EC of compulsory major and core study, a 15-EC Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC USE/Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of free electives. The compulsory formation integrates anatomy, physiology, molecular and cell biology, chemistry, disease mechanisms and medical applications with mathematics, physics, programming, biomedical data, imaging, materials, laboratory research and challenge-based technology development. The complete 105/15/15/45 allocation is retained below rather than assigning unsupported individual credit values to topic and learning-line lists.

alternatives.concept: Builds a biomedical-science pathway from molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, anatomy and physiology into genetics, disease mechanisms, infection, pharmacology, laboratory investigation, epidemiology and quantitative evidence. It is the closest feasible UCR response to the medically oriented TU/e major, while not reproducing its physics, biomaterials, biomedical instrumentation, engineering-design or required final-project sequence.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest programme, programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, image processing, neural networks and robotics replace epidemiology, infection and immunity, neurobiology, perception and action, medical and health psychology, and lifespan developmental psychology. alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible 24-course response to the medically oriented major's molecular, cellular, physiological, disease, treatment, laboratory and evidence base. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit biomedical-data, imaging and diagnosis cluster and passes all feasibility and pairwise-distinctness rules. A regenerative-medicine, biomaterials and medical-technology-design direction was also tested, but UCR lacks the materials, tissue-engineering, biofabrication and device-design sequence needed to sustain it as a third programme.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine directly addresses the programme's integrated medical and life-science foundation, but not its full engineering and technology scope.
Ethics provides normative analysis relevant to responsible medical technology, but does not reproduce TU/e's complete technology-specific USE/Impact of Technology formation.

TU/e requires a 15-EC biomedical Bachelor Final Project; no scheduled UCR course is treated as equivalent, and UCR's standardized optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately by the compiler.
TU/e preserves 45 EC of genuine free elective choice; it is not filled with match-optimising invented content.

notes.text: TU/e Medical Sciences and Engineering integrates medical science with physics, chemistry, programming, biomedical data, imaging, biomaterials, laboratory work, challenge-based technology development and a required 15-EC Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers strong molecular and cellular biology, physiology, anatomy, disease, pharmacology, one life-science laboratory, mathematics, data science and imaging-related computation, but neither alternative reproduces TU/e's physics, biomaterials, tissue engineering, biomedical instrumentation, medical-device design, staged engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. TU/e also preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space.
